findings.title: Keep the frozen result types in sync with `OpResultArtifactSchema`.

findings.body:
**Reject author self-closure in `AcceptancePayloadSchema`.**

`AcceptancePayloadSchema` has no refinement. It accepts `independent: true` when `reviewerId` equals `authorId`. The documented contract says author closure is never independent acceptance (`src/kernel/types.ts:809`). The schema header says documented couplings are encoded as refinements, not prose (`src/kernel/schema.ts:21`). This schema is the only check on the record, and it is used by the head-acceptance journal event and the report's `acceptances` array.

The acceptance writer is disabled and the importer is deferred (`src/kernel/types.ts:821`). The gap is therefore latent today, but any record that reaches this schema with equal identities would be reported as independent acceptance.

<details>
<summary>🛡️ Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
     availability: AvailabilityMapSchema,
   })
-  .strict();
+  .strict()
+  .refine((payload) => !(payload.independent && payload.reviewerId === payload.authorId), {
+    message: 'Author closure is never independent acceptance',
+    path: ['independent'],
+  });
```

</details>

Check the fixture at `test/measurement-acceptance.test.ts:105` against the new rule. Its contents were not inspected.
findings.title: Reject author self-closure in `AcceptancePayloadSchema`.

findings.body:
**Close the withdrawal only when every judged measurement was a non-tightening skip.**

The withdrawal gate at `proposeBaselineUpdate.ts:839` matches the substring `not a tightening` in skip reasons. Two other skip reasons can embed file-derived text. The identity-disagreement reason embeds `baseline.target` from the parsed file. The corrupt-baseline reason embeds the parse error message. If a committed baseline carries that phrase in one of those fields, and every other judged metric is a non-tightening skip, an open proposal is closed. The comment at lines 835-836 says corrupt baselines must not close a proposal.

`restored` receives an entry only on the non-tightening branch. When `applied.length === 0`, each judged measurement produces exactly one skip. `restored.length === judged.length` therefore selects the same cases without matching message text.

<details>
<summary>🐛 Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
       if (
         judged.length > 0 &&
-        skipped.every((entry) => entry.reason.includes('not a tightening'))
+        restored.length === judged.length
       ) {
```

</details>
